cards.explanation: The answer is True. Peter says he is "…a witness of Christ’s sufferings…" (1 Peter 5:1). He isn't talking about suffering from far away, either. He writes to people in a hard season as someone who saw Christ's sufferings. He also adds that he's a partaker of the glory to be revealed, so the suffering isn't the end of his sentence.

The answer is shepherds of God's flock. Peter says, "Be shepherds of God’s flock that is among you…" (1 Peter 5:2). A shepherd watches over the sheep. He doesn't just stand there and point at them. And notice that the flock is God's, friends, so the elders are looking after something that belongs to Him.

The answer is False. Peter says the elders are to watch over the flock "not out of greed, but out of eagerness…" (1 Peter 5:2). Greed is what he rules out. He wants them eager to serve, and I think that's a much better motive than chasing a payday.

The answer is examples to the flock. Peter says, "…not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock." (1 Peter 5:3). The elders lead by showing the way, not by bossing people around. An example is something the flock can see.

The answer is False. Peter says the crown of glory "…will never fade away." (1 Peter 5:4). He says it will come when the Chief Shepherd appears. I can't say that about anything I've ever pulled out of an oven.

The answer is submit to them. Peter says, "Young men, in the same way, submit yourselves to your elders." (1 Peter 5:5). The elders are told to be examples, and the young men are told to submit. Each group gets its own job.

The word is proud. Peter quotes, "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble." (1 Peter 5:5). Notice the two sides of it, friends: grace goes to the humble, and opposition goes to the proud. I'd rather be on the grace side.

The answer is True. Peter says, "Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you." (1 Peter 5:7). He gives the reason right there in the verse: He cares for you. So you can hand the worry over.

The answer is someone to devour. Peter says the adversary prowls around like a roaring lion, "…seeking someone to devour." (1 Peter 5:8). That's why Peter says to be sober-minded and alert. A lion that roars is hard to ignore, and I'd stay awake too.

The answer is to resist him and stand firm. Peter says, "Resist him, standing firm in your faith…" (1 Peter 5:9). He doesn't tell them to run or to bargain. He tells them to stand, and to stand in their faith.

The answer is True. Peter says to stand firm "…in the knowledge that your brothers throughout the world are undergoing the same kinds of suffering." (1 Peter 5:9). That's worth knowing when a trial feels lonely, friends. Peter's readers aren't the only ones in it, because their brothers throughout the world are in it too.

The answer is that He will restore and strengthen them. Peter says the God of all grace "…will Himself restore you, secure you, strengthen you, and establish you." (1 Peter 5:10). That's four promises in one verse. And notice the word Himself: God does it personally.
The answer is False. Peter says, "…after you have suffered for a little while…" God will restore them (1 Peter 5:10). The words are a little while. He doesn't say it will drag on.

The answer is Silvanus. Peter writes, "Through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly…" (1 Peter 5:12). Peter calls him a faithful brother. That's a good thing to have on your record.
